fact_text: Systems Limited was founded in 1977 by Babar Ali and listed on the PSX through an IPO at the end of 2014.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems is presented as the flagship of Pakistan's IT services exporters, and its core work is outsourced IT services for banks and telecom operators.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems holds first right of refusal for Temenos central-bank software implementations in the GCC and Asia-Pacific, so it can match the best tender bid and win the contract.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects the Temenos-linked banking software segment to become Systems' largest revenue generator over time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' revenue was about PKR 7.5 billion in 2019, of which about PKR 2.7 billion came from the GCC.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' 2025 revenue was projected at about PKR 80 billion, of which roughly PKR 50 billion was expected to come from the Middle East.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Around two-thirds of the roughly PKR 70 billion revenue increase between 2019 and 2025 was attributed to Middle East clients, which makes the region the key growth driver.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Middle East IT contracts are typically USD 10 to 20 million, far smaller than the billion-dollar deals of large US and European clients, which the analyst sees as a more accessible market for Systems.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Saudi Arabia was described as the next growth leg for Systems, after the company had nearly the largest stall at the LEAP 2024 exhibition.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Egypt is presented as the lowest-cost Arabic-speaking delivery centre, so Systems hires Arabic speakers there to serve Middle East clients while shifting some staff away from Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems is described as professionally run, with most shareholders being long-serving former employees rather than founding family members.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems runs a training programme that takes non-IT graduates and gives them IT skills in 3 to 6 months, to close Pakistan's shortage of IT graduates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT services are capital-light: the main investments are offices and working capital rather than plant or machinery, so returns on new client revenue can be high.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT service firms are typically paid 60 to 90 days after invoicing, so growing revenue requires working capital that ties up cash before collections arrive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst ranks return on invested capital (ROIC), including working capital, as the metric to focus on when hunting for long-term compounders in IT services.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT firms may book salaries under admin expenses or cost of sales, so gross margin can be inflated by classification; operating profit after all costs is the fairer comparison.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 40% rule adds operating margin and revenue growth rate; a total above 40% marks a high-growth company that global investors favour.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' quarterly profit swings with its share of profit or loss from associates, which come from startup investments, so the analyst strips these out to judge the core business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Management guided for 20% to 25% revenue growth in USD terms in 2025, which implies revenue of roughly PKR 80 to 85 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' 2025 net profit was projected at roughly PKR 9 to 10 billion after all expenses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' market value of about PKR 150 billion equated to roughly 15 to 16 times the 2025 earnings expected at the time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 15 to 16 times earnings multiple looks high to the analyst, but could be justified if profit keeps growing over the following two years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT exporters bill clients in dollars but pay staff in rupees, so a stronger rupee compresses margins unless fixed-price contracts are repriced.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Systems' margins fell because contracts were negotiated on an expected stronger dollar rate, and the company is gradually renegotiating those contracts after the rupee held steady.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because its clients are foreign and it imports little, Systems is largely insulated from Pakistan's domestic shocks, and it captures little benefit when the domestic outlook improves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Higher salary tax rates raise IT service costs, because employees judge offers on after-tax pay while the company prices contracts on pre-tax salary cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IT exporters and freelancers are allowed to repatriate 50% of export proceeds in dollars, and retained dollars can fund purchases of foreign companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the new dollar rules, a Pakistani IT firm can buy a foreign company, take over its clients and shift its cost base to Pakistan, a route to growth beyond organic rates of 20 to 30%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Paying for acquisitions with new shares dilutes existing holders, so a cash-generative IT firm should pay in cash, and Buffett's test compares each deal with the acquirer's existing businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A tax on IT export profits would cut fair value and ROIC; the analyst thinks it unlikely, but a similar tax on goods exporters such as Interloop shows the risk is real.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's low labour cost for software and IT services is the main reason exporters win global contracts against higher-cost rivals.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Middle East revenue growth and Middle East operating margin are the two indicators to track in each quarterly result, since they determine whether the business is on course.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A share can lag strong revenue growth when margins compress from currency effects and a high P/E multiple normalises toward a typical range.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Systems Limited - Pakistan's No.1 IT Exporter' (YouTube transcript, undated)
